name: Retsin
label: Simple Machines
lede: Tara Jane O'Neil and Cynthia Nelson met on the road in 1993, each in a different touring band. Two years later they were on Simple Machines with an 8-track record, and by 2001 they'd swapped electric guitars for banjo, flute and toy piano.

eras.title: Two vans cross paths
eras.text: Tara Jane O'Neil played bass and sang in Louisville's Rodan; Cynthia Nelson played in Ruby Falls. Their bands were on the road at the same time in 1993, and by 1994 the two of them were a couple and a band, working around their day jobs.

years.h: Rodan's Tara Jane O'Neil meets Ruby Falls' Cynthia Nelson on tour
years.p: Both bands were out on national tours in 1993. AllMusic says the two became a couple in 1994 and started making music together.

years.h: Half-Cocked, a road movie about a stolen van, casts them both
years.p: Filmed in Louisville, Nashville and Chattanooga, it follows teenagers who take a band's van and gear. O'Neil and Nelson act in it, with Rodan, Unwound and Polvo playing themselves.
years.xp:
Half-Cocked mixes actors with real indie bands, so the cast list doubles as a map of the mid-90s underground: Slant 6, Helium, Versus and Freakwater are in it too. Wikipedia lists O'Neil as herself, credited as Rhonda, and Nelson as herself. Ian Svenonius plays her brother Otis.

Suki Hawley directed. It came out in 1994 as a limited VHS run and stayed unavailable for years, until a 2007 DVD.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tara Jane O'Neil · Wikipedia: Retsin
years.h: Rodan ends, and O'Neil moves to New York
years.p: Wikipedia dates the end of [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]] to 1994. O'Neil relocated to New York and put her time into Retsin and other projects, including the Sonora Pine.

eras.title: Salt Lick, then Egg Fusion
eras.text: Retsin landed on Simple Machines, the DC-area label run by Tsunami's Jenny Toomey and Kristin Thomson, and put out two records in two years. Both were made by two people passing instruments back and forth, with friends filling in.

years.src: Discogs: Salt Lick · Wikipedia: Retsin · AllMusic: Retsin
years.h: Salt Lick starts on one 8-track in Louisville
years.p: Recording began in September 1994 on a single 8-track in Louisville, then moved to New York and, in February 1995, to WGNS Studios in DC. It came out as Simple Machines SMR 42.
years.xp:
The credits list Nelson and O'Neil on guitar, bass and vocals, with Steve Thornton on trombone, Jennifer Sharpe on steel guitar and Geoff Turner on guitar feedback and piano.

Discogs lists it as an eight-track CD EP; Wikipedia calls it their debut album. AllMusic gives the debut to Egg Fusion instead.

years.h: Egg Fusion: 14 songs from a house on Goddard Avenue
years.p: Recorded in October 1995 as Simple Machines SMR 46. O'Neil plays drums, keyboards and ocarina as well as guitar and bass.
years.xp: Per the liner notes, most tracks came from the Goddard Avenue house in Louisville. A few, like Duck Out, are 4-track recordings made in New York and Louisville. It was mixed at Falk Recording Studio.

years.h: Touring behind Salt Lick, with a rhythm section when one turns up
years.p: Wikipedia says they toured extensively behind the first record. Some nights they added a rhythm section; often it was just the two of them.
years.xp: This set was taped upstairs at the Middle East in Cambridge, Massachusetts, on May 2, 1995, going by the upload's title.

eras.title: A label closes, the guitars go quiet
eras.text: Simple Machines shut down in 1998 and Retsin moved to Chicago's Carrot Top Records. The duo leaned further into folk instruments.

years.h: Sweet Luck of Amaryllis, the first record for Carrot Top
years.p: Todd Cook plays bass, with Tony Bailey and Greta Ritcher on drums for two songs. Temporary Residence also pressed it on vinyl as TRR 14.
years.xp: Reviewer Matt Dornan called it an album for lonely, rainy afternoons and picked out the opener, Lone Star Drive. AllMusic places the group's move from guitar rock toward folk instruments in the years after Simple Machines closed.

years.h: When Simple Machines folds, Retsin goes to Chicago
years.p: The label went out of business in 1998, and the band landed at Carrot Top Records.

years.h: By now the guitars are mostly gone
years.p: AllMusic describes them as a capable neo-folk outfit, working with banjo, accordion, violin and flute instead of standard rock instruments.

years.h: Ida and Retsin share a record, billed as a family
years.p: The Ida Retsin Family Volume One teams the duo with the New York band Ida, on Muss My Hair Records.

eras.title: Cabin in the woods
eras.text: The last stretch was quiet and pastoral. Retsin made one more album, then both women joined Anna Padgett in a new band.

yt: Cabin in the Woods, full album
years.h: Cabin in the Woods: banjo, flute and toy piano
years.p: O'Neil plays guitar, banjo, toy piano and vocals; Nelson plays guitar, flute and vocals. Carrot Top released it in the US, with editions in France and Japan.
years.xp: Christian Quick mixed and mastered it, and O'Neil made the artwork. It is Retsin's last full-length.

years.h: The Moon Money Moon EP ends the discography
years.p: Acuarela Discos of Spain put it out in 2001. Wikipedia lists it as the last Retsin release.

years.h: O'Neil and Nelson join Anna Padgett in Naysayer
years.p: The new band made two albums, in 2001 and 2002. Retsin's story stops there.

eras.title: After Retsin
eras.text: O'Neil went solo in 2000 with Peregrine and has kept making records and visual art since.

years.p: The 2000 debut on Quarterstick began a solo run that reaches 2024's The Cool Cloud of Okayness, on labels including K and Kranky.
years.xp: She is also a visual artist, with work shown in New York, Barcelona, Tokyo, Kyoto and Louisville, among other places. Her art has appeared on covers for Ida and Castanets.
